They are not a current provider-versus-provider choice and are not merely stale historical reason strings. Details and exact failing predicates follow.

**Eight current held candidates carry “Sources disagree on the title or author”, but none retains a current provider-versus-provider choice.** Every current result has only `sources.kind=local_agreement`, a local work/review, no saved competing provider field/value proposal, and null `wait`/`gap_wait`. This does not prove an earlier disagreement never happened and does not authorize clearing a hold. No defensible provider A/provider B question can be prepared from these stored records. Keep the holds and report missing evidence. A local-title/spelling confirmation can be offered separately and labelled accurately; it must not be presented as resolving an unseen provider contradiction.

## Identity ambiguity versus unavailable evidence

The separately counted three **Book identity uncertain** holds are not included in these eight. This report does not relabel them or select identities for them. The eight above have generic conflict reasons and current locally agreed identity. Missing original title/series is a metadata gap; transliteration or a narrator-like album-artist credit is not evidence of a second provider identity. The app needs to expose the real conflicting field, each proposed value, source URL/provider and retrieval/identity binding when it actually has them.

For the eight scoped title fragments, exact URL substring searches of `public_research_cache` found no retained matching request bodies. Matching the historical response hashes found only repeated unrelated OpenLibrary response bodies, so a shared response hash cannot recover a title/author proposal for these books. No provider was contacted; unavailable **stored evidence** must not be reported as current network/provider unavailability.

## Read method and reproducibility

Opened `file:C:/Antigravity Projects/Studio Illuminati/WIP/Books Arranger/data/inventory.sqlite3?mode=ro` with SQLite URI mode, set `PRAGMA query_only=ON` and `BEGIN`. Never imported the application/scanner or invoked its setup/write paths. The existing catalog was not copied or booted. Revision-current hold selection joined `automatic_candidates a` to `book_groups g` on `id`, `revision` and `fingerprint`, required `g.superseded=0` and `a.state='Held'`, then selected the exact reason through `json_each(a.result,'$.reasons')`. That snapshot yielded 65 current Held rows and 8 with the exact disagreement reason. Raw historical Held rows are a different scope and were not substituted.

Read the selected eight saved results, local clues, evidence, proposals and retained research histories; revision-current candidate contexts and canonical reviews were absent for all eight. A final read at 07:38:49.971647Z confirmed all eight IDs, revision 2, matching group/result fingerprints and Held state unchanged. No whole-library inventory or audio re-audit was performed.

Python `C:/Python314/python.exe -B` ran through the existing native owned supervisor with a finite 600000 ms bound; successful reads closed with native active=0. One initial full-held-result payload exceeded its fixed output budget, was refused/closed and was replaced with compact scoped queries. No limit was bypassed and no evidence was inferred from truncated output. UTF-8 console ambiguity was avoided by ASCII-escaped JSON transport.

## Implemented local-gate correction and verification

Authorized follow-on implementation changes only `source_identity.py`, a small pure helper in `local_identity.py`, and `tests/test_local_gate_consistency.py`. Existing successful filename checks remain accepted; the local-only fallback reuses the same whole-filename/title-segment and bounded spelling-slip comparison already used by local agreement. Different volume digits remain different. Genuine person-like filename author credits still must match the work. A numeric-position prefix is treated as a source/cycle label only when an actual embedded author matches the canonical work aliases. Unknown/nonmatching embedded authors, narrator markers and arbitrary non-person credits do not become authors. Explicit narrator aliases in the established narrator-collection route retain their existing behavior. Public/provider identity paths keep the strict original filename rule. Source availability, membership, order, track totals, format and explicit conflicting author tags remain independently checked.

The new policy marker is `source_identity.LOCAL_SOURCE_GATE_VERSION = "local-source-gate-v2"`; the legacy `VERSION` and grouping algorithm identity are unchanged. Primary Ender owns persisting that marker in automatic result records and supported old-policy held-candidate re-evaluation with exact source revision/fingerprint and manual evidence/editing-lease protections. No blanket database reset or silent approval is part of this slice. Existing live holds remain as stored until the reviewed new app explicitly rechecks them through supported controls/automatic policy refresh.
